Competent

KOM-pih-tunt — think 'complete the tent': a competent camper can complete the tent setup without help. · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Competent is having the skill and knowledge needed to do something successfully.

The new nurse proved competent, handling every patient calmly and correctly.

Worked Example

On her first solo night shift, the technician notices the server crash immediately. She diagnoses the problem, restores the backups, and documents every step. No supervisor ever needs to be called.

She has all the skill and knowledge the job requires — she is competent. Unlike 'brilliant,' which implies extraordinary talent, competent means fully capable of doing the job well.

How Competent Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

capable

capable: having the ability to do something

skilled

skilled: having expertise from training or practice

qualified

qualified: meeting the requirements for a task

Antonyms

incompetent

incompetent: lacking the ability to do something properly

clumsy

clumsy: awkward and lacking skill at a task

How Strong Is It? — adequate → competent → masterful

adequate vs. competent

adequate vs. competent: Adequate is weaker than competent — an adequate worker is barely good enough, while a competent one is solidly and reliably capable.

masterful vs. competent

masterful vs. competent: Masterful is stronger than competent: a competent musician plays the piece correctly, but a masterful one commands it at an expert level.

Build the Word

The pieces

prefix — com-

prefix — com-: together (Latin)

root — pet-

root — pet-: to seek, to strive (Latin)

suffix — -ent

suffix — -ent: in a state of (adjective-forming) (Latin)

Put it together

Put it together: Latin competere meant 'to strive together, to be fitting.' Someone whose skills 'come together' to fit a task is suitable for it — competent.
